answer: A restoration exchange auctions work on a juniper terrace beside a shifting dune. Before bidding, each agent must earn a nontransferable permit through a probation job checked by an independent inspector, then lock a performance bond. One permit supports one active crew, so ten fresh aliases require ten probation jobs, crews and bonds; false reports can forfeit the bonds. A wealthy operator can still hire real crews, and a cartel could fake inspections, so rotate inspectors, audit site records and allow appeals for honest entrants.
